title: Northstride Logistics - Renewal & Expansion Readout
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on expanding committed capacity, adding EU region and validating VPC/on-prem options for sensitive routing. Customer wants predictable latency for last-mile inference and clearer billing cadence. Redwood team to supply security pack, revised pricing for dedicated burst nodes, and an onboarding runbook for EU VPC activation.
topics: Current usage patterns and projected growth (Q4-Q1)
Dedicated vs hosted recommendation for latency-sensitive routes
EU region onboarding and VPC/private deployment considerations
Pricing model for committed capacity + burst
SLA/Compliance (SOC2, audit logs, KMS) and procurement ask
action_items: Ava Chen - Send revised committed capacity pricing and 12/24 month options by 2026-10-07
Luis Moreno - Share EU VPC runbook + network diagram and required peering info by 2026-10-08
Priya Patel - Schedule 1:1 onboarding session with Omar for SRE playbook (target 2026-10-12)
Maya Singh - Provide projected peak RPS and 99th pct latency target for checkout flow by 2026-10-06

Customer to provide telemetry sample (10k requests) for Redwood SE to run quick latency profiling

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Ava, Luis, Priya (Redwood); Evan, Maya, Omar, Zoe (Northstride)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick renewal chat turned into expansion planning — customer wants committed uplift and EU VPC pilot; procurement and SRE involved.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining — happy Friday. quick agenda: renewal numbers, eu region onboarding, and security questions.
[00:16] Evan Hart: Thanks Ava, yeah we want to go over capacity numbers, and make sure the EU deploy won't break our latency targets for last-mile. we ran some smoke tests last month and saw spikes.
[00:30] Maya Singh: Hi all, i'll be focusing on SLA and on the engineering requirements — thanks for making time.
[00:38] Luis Moreno: Yeah hi, Luis here, i'll walk through the dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and also what the private/VPC flow looks like from our side.
[00:45] Priya Patel: and i'll own the onboarding timeline and ops playbook.
[00:50] Zoe Lin: quick note from procurement: we'll need the redlineable contract and PO terms, also confirmation on egress billing for EU.
[01:05] Ava Chen: Perfect, i'll follow-up with pricing options. can you confirm current committed nodes and current token/month estimate?
[01:18] Omar Reyes: We're on the hosted plan today, roughly 40M tokens/month across inference and embeddings, but peak windows are nasty — up to 2k rps for the routing service.
[01:32] Evan Hart: yeah those peaks are what push us to think dedicated. our 99th percentile latency requirement for checkout is 200ms end-to-end, we want inference below 80ms ideally.
[01:48] Luis Moreno: okay so for 80ms inference p99 that's typically a dedicated path on Nvidia A100 class or equivalent — but we also have quantized options. the trade is cost vs throughput; dedicated gives predictable latency and KV cache warmness, hosted is cheaper but you see jitter.
[02:05] Maya Singh: how deterministic is your fallback policy? if dedicated goes down do requests route to hosted automatically? we don't want increased latencies during failover.
[02:16] Luis Moreno: yes — we have smart routing, we can set policies to failover to compatible model variants in a different region, and there's knob to prefer low latency. there's a short step-up in latency during cold failover but we can pre-warm KV cache with traffic mirroring for critical routes.
[02:33] Evan Hart: traffic mirroring — is that something we can do into a staging cluster in eu to pre-warm before cutover?
[02:40] Priya Patel: absolutely, we typically run a 2-week pre-warm and mirroring window. for EU onboarding we recommend a pilot with 2 dedicated nodes and prefix caching enabled.
[02:52] Zoe Lin: about data residency and encryption — we need SOC 2 type II, KMS integration, and proof of audit logs retention for at least 1 year.
[03:05] Ava Chen: Redwood is SOC2 attested, we support customer-managed KMS via our Private offering and we can provide audit log exports. i'll drop the security pack with specifics.
[03:16] Maya Singh: can you share the exact KMS flow? we use AWS KMS and have strict key rotation policies, also HSM is preferred on certain flows.
[03:25] Luis Moreno: we integrate with AWS KMS for Private deployments and support bring-your-own-key. HSM-backed KMS via partner stacks is possible on the dedicated/private tier — i'll include network diagrams and heatmap of egress in the runbook. small note: our doc sometimes shows K V cash spelled wrong in the auto transcript but we mean KV cache.
[03:46] Omar Reyes: hahah yeah we've seen K V cash once.
[03:50] Ava Chen: side topic: billing — you're interested in committed capacity with burst. we'll show 12m and 24m commitment tiers and burst node pricing. any preference on billing cadence monthly vs quarterly?
[04:06] Zoe Lin: monthly invoicing is preferred but we can do quarterly if there's a discount threshold. procurement needs to know the exact CLINs for PO.
[04:15] Evan Hart: timeline: we want EU in prod by late Nov, ideally. is that feasible?
[04:22] Priya Patel: late Nov is tight but feasible if we start pilot next week. pilot 2 weeks, then 1 week of validation, then staged rollout. that puts us right at the end of November.
[04:35] Maya Singh: Ok, what do you need from us to get the pilot started?
[04:39] Luis Moreno: we'll need network peering details, sample telemetry (10k requests), and a list of top 3 latency-sensitive routes. also a contact for peering engineer.
[04:52] Evan Hart: we can get that — Omar and I will produce telemetry and doc.
[04:58] Zoe Lin: also, on contract amendments: do you have a template for committed capacity addendum? our legal prefers a shorter SOW + amendment rather than whole contract replacement.
[05:10] Ava Chen: yes we have a commitment addendum template, i'll share with Zoe and legal.
[05:16] Omar Reyes: technical deep-dive question — what's your KV cache warm-up behavior in cross-region seeding? we saw cache misses when we originally spun up EU nodes.
[05:27] Luis Moreno: seed behavior depends on prefix caching and whether you mirror requests; out-of-the-box cold caches will have misses. we recommend request mirroring for critical prefixes and use sticky routing during warm-up. also using lower-precision quantization on less-sensitive routes helps keep throughput high without latency penalty.
[05:48] Maya Singh: show us numbers — can you give expected p99 numbers for the pilot setup?
[05:53] Luis Moreno: for dedicated EU nodes, expected inference p50 ~ 15-25ms, p95 ~ 45-60ms, p99 ~ 75-110ms depending on model size and sequence length. with KV cache warm and optimized kernels you'll be on the lower end.
[06:12] Evan Hart: that's promising. cost — what kind of delta are we looking at vs hosted?
[06:17] Ava Chen: approximate: hosted might be 20-35% cheaper for baseline throughput, but with unpredictable jitter. Dedicated committed nodes give a predictable monthly unit price and we can model cost per million tokens in the proposal. burst capacity is priced add-on.
[06:34] Zoe Lin: procurement will require a finalized estimate to sign PO. can you produce a best-estimate by next Wednesday?
[06:42] Ava Chen: yes, i'll produce committed 12/24 month options with expected monthly invoices and a line for burst.
[06:48] Priya Patel: i'll take point on the onboarding schedule and coordinate with Omar for the SRE playbook session.
[06:55] Omar Reyes: great, we also want a playback of fallback behavior in a rehearsal — can we do a staged failover test during pilot?
[07:03] Luis Moreno: yes, we can run failover drills and we'll include a runbook for traffic mirroring and pre-warm.
[07:12] Maya Singh: one more ask — model governance. do you provide model version pinning and rollbacks? we need the ability to pin a commit and rollback quickly if quality regresses.
[07:22] Luis Moreno: yes, Redwood supports model version pinning, A/B and canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. we can also add quality monitoring tied to a prompt set to watch for regressions.
[07:36] Evan Hart: sounds good. any blockers on your side?
[07:39] Ava Chen: none — next is to get the sample telemetry and legal contact. we'll follow up with the pricing deck, security pack, and EU runbook.
[07:48] Zoe Lin: ok i'll confirm legal contact and PO timeline by Friday.
[07:52] Ava Chen: recap: Redwood sends pricing & addendum, SE sends EU runbook and heatmap, CS schedules onboarding session, Northstride provides telemetry + legal contact. target pilot kickoff next week.
[08:08] Maya Singh: thanks everyone.
[08:11] (call ends)
